mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (GDPC1) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the interaction signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% year-over-year suggests accelerating consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are negative despite the signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 suggests supply-side softness, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with a p-value < 0.05 over the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL), it signals a strong labor market and disinflation, leading to positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < previous month
regime_hint: labor market strengthening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs without a corresponding increase in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, predicting positive S&P 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 and UNRATE remains flat or declines in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are negative with a significant interaction effect (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) of 5% or more is a leading indicator of supply-side weakness and is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with a statistically significant signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPI inflation exceeds 2% in a month preceding the decision, it suggests persistent price pressures and is associated with negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with a p-value > 0.05 when inflation accelerates.
